journal.title: Wed Sep 30 review: -$35 (the MUU call); Thursday: sell the call, VICR on confirmation, NKE calls at 3:55
journal.body:

What didn't work: the call was bought at 9:56 AM, so it paid a full day of time decay and implied-vol premium while MU went nowhere. The paper fill used the options.json ask ($2.90), $0.15 above Robinhood's live ask. Lesson: for event options, buy close to the event (the NKE plan buys at 3:55 PM), and re-sync the chain right before the fill so the price is current.

journal.title: Bought 1 MUU Oct 2 $37 call at $2.90 ($290) ahead of Micron's report
journal.body:
Per plans J0007 and J0010. At 9:56 AM MU was $1,069 (+0.3%), which meets the 'flat or up' condition; MUU was $36.88.
Robinhood read-only check at 9:56: bid 2.60 / ask 2.75 (185 contracts offered), implied vol 233%, delta 0.53, theta -0.60 a day, break-even $39.68, chance of profit 32%, open interest 972. Our paper fill uses the ask in options.json ($2.90), $0.15 worse than Robinhood's ask, which passes the 5% check. Break-even at our price is $39.90, 8.2% above MUU, so Micron needs to rise about 4%.
Chose the 37 strike over the 38: it fits the $300 budget and has more delta (0.53 vs 0.47) for about $60 more.
Size: 29% of the book; a total loss costs $290. The implied move is in line with history, so this is a bounded bet on direction, not an edge.
Exits (one contract, so no thirds): on a gap down, sell at Thursday's first regular-session run. On a gap up, sell by the 11:55 AM run at the latest, earlier if the call is worth $5.80 (+100%) or more at any run. Never held into Friday: Robinhood force-closes at 3:30 PM Friday.

journal.title: GPUS (Hyperscale Data): avoid; the company is the seller
journal.body: The user asked about GPUS (Hyperscale Data, formerly Ault Alliance). Deep dive in research/dossiers/GPUS-2026-09-29.md. Verdict: avoid in both books. The decline is mechanical. The company sells stock continuously through its at-the-market program (Class A shares 323M to 581M in the first half, then 70.8M more by Aug 13 for $9.2M). Six reverse splits since 2019 multiply to about 1-for-1.05 billion, and the price is back under NYSE American's $0.20 low-price line. Ahead of common: about $275M of liabilities (including $99M of notes due within a year) and $91M of preferred with monthly cash dividends. The auditors' going-concern doubt stands, and the company made a $5M loan to its controlling shareholder in June. The "cash + Bitcoin = 153% of market cap" release counts pledged Bitcoin and restricted cash and ignores those claims.

journal.title: GNRC: outside report checked; no trade inside the window
journal.body:
The user shared an outside research report on Generac (4 pages); its main question is whether Generac can deliver its data center orders on time and at good margins. Checked against filings and price data:
- Confirmed: Amazon agreement worth up to $8B, about $2.4B of initial deliveries expected in 2027-28; Amazon warrant for 1,693,745 shares at $200.93 (about 2.9% of 59.1M shares); 52-week high $296.44; 48.8x trailing earnings.
- The "+40% after hours" is the after-hours peak: $255 at 4:45 PM on Sep 16 (+46% on thin volume). The stock opened +31% on Sep 17, closed +18.3% at $207.23, and has traded $198-212 since. The market priced the news within hours and sold off the overshoot.
- 48x is on trailing GAAP EPS of $4.35. On consensus forward EPS of $12.47 it is 17x, close to Cummins (15x) and below Caterpillar (25.5x), Vertiv (27x), Eaton (27x) and Powell (27x). A multiples-based fair value comes down to two choices. Which earnings: does $12.47 hold without the Q2 tariff refund and after the warrant cost? Which peers: 15x (generator maker) gives about $188; 26-27x (data center power suppliers) gives about $330. At $212 the market prices Generac as a generator maker, not yet as a data center supplier.
- "Up to $8B" is the ceiling for warrant vesting, not a firm order; the expected part is about $2.4B.
- Warrants given to a customer are booked as a reduction of revenue as they vest. My rough Black-Scholes value is about $118 per warrant share ($207 price, 7-year life, 50% volatility), about $200M in total, or roughly 2.5% of $8B: a price concession to Amazon on top of the dilution.
Decision: every checkpoint (Q3 results Oct 28, capacity build-out to Q3 2027) falls after Oct 5, and the jump study shows no average follow-through for jumps like this. No Generac trade in either book; it stays on the watchlist.

journal.title: Evidence check: 241 jumps, noise rule, no $1 floor, breakout triggers withdrawn
journal.body:
Tested on 241 one-day jumps (15% or more, at least 2x volume) across 3,914 NYSE/Nasdaq/NYSE American stocks with no share-price floor, market cap of at least $30M and at least $0.5M traded a day, Aug 18 to Sep 29. Returns are measured against SPY (scripts/jump_study.py, research/movers/study-2026-09-29.json).

- All jumps: median -3.0% over the next 5 sessions and -5.1% over 10. Buying the day after a jump lost to the market in the typical case; the gains sit in a minority of names.
- Noise, the user's volatility idea: stocks with one-year volatility of 120% or more, or 10 or more +/-15% days in the prior year, fell a median 15.7% over 10 sessions, and half lost more than 15%. The rest fell 4.1%. Rule adopted: skip those stocks. A stricter first version (4 or more such days) would have excluded IOVA, VICR and FEIM for no gain.
- Share price: under $1 was no worse than $1-5 (10-session medians -5.6% and -5.1%). The $1 floor was the wrong filter and is gone.
- Market cap: under $100M, median -13.2% over 10 sessions, and 19 of 40 lost more than 15%. Still scanned for visibility, but scored -3.
- Calm stocks of $100M or more with fundamental news (71 jumps): median +0.3% at 5 sessions and -2.4% at 10; 7 of 55 gained more than 15% and 4 lost more than 15%. On average the market priced the news on day one.
- Entry timing, calm stocks of $100M or more: buying at the first new post-jump closing high did worse than buying at the jump-day close (5-session median -2.2% vs -1.1%, up in 21 of 61 vs 52 of 117).

Decision: the breakout triggers in J0013/J0004 (GNRC above $213, VICR above $292, SEI above $71, FEIM above $89) are withdrawn. These names stay on watch without a buy rule. The scan feeds research, not this week's entries. Scheduled catalysts (Micron, Nike, the jobs report) and the positions we hold stay the plan.

Caveats: one market regime, overlapping windows, 10-session horizon, and only stocks still listed and above the size floor today (survivors), which flatters the small caps.

journal.title: 30-session jump scan: evidence and four candidates
journal.body:
Universe: 3,294 US stocks (market cap >= $100M, price >= $1, 3-month average volume > 200K). In the last 30 sessions, 154 of them had a one-day jump of 15% or more on at least 2x normal volume (scripts/movers.py --lookback 30, saved to research/movers/lookback-2026-09-29.json).

What they did after the jump, to the Sep 29 close: holding (kept the jump, no further run) 69, extending (+15% or more beyond the jump-day close) 34, fading 20, round-trip (gave back the whole jump) 27, new 4.

By cause of the jump:
- Fundamental news (guidance, earnings, contract, refinancing, trial or approval), 76 names: median -0.8% since the jump. 15 extended, 39 held, 12 faded, 10 round-tripped.
- No clear news, 35 names: median +0.3%. The mean is +20.6%, carried by a few micro-cap pumps (WCT, TJGC, USDE, GLND).
So jumps on real news usually hold (51 of 76 held or extended), but the typical name does not keep drifting within a few weeks; the gains come from the roughly one in five that extend. The news gives the candidate list; the price has to confirm. Caveats: one month, one market regime, not adjusted for the market, jumps of different ages.

Candidates at or near the post-jump high, catalyst checked at the source:
- GNRC $212.22: $8B agreement to supply backup generators for Amazon data centers (Sep 16), about $2.4B of deliveries in 2027-28. Amazon received warrants for up to 1.69M shares at $200.93, vesting with purchases. The contract is about 1.8x Generac's annual revenue. Jumped 18.3% on Sep 17 (close about $207.2); now at its highest close since. Average analyst target $289.
- VICR $290.68: raised its Q3 sequential growth guide from about 10% to more than 20%, driven by royalties from a Vertical Power Delivery license to a leading AI OEM; four OEMs or hyperscalers now hold licenses. Jumped 19.8% on Sep 22 (close $268.34); at its highest close since. Target $386.
- SEI $68.34: Q3 adjusted EBITDA guide raised to $110-130M (was $90-105M), Q4 to $145-180M (was $100-120M), and a first Q1 2027 guide of $200-240M. Jumped 16.3% on Sep 8; 3.8% below its highest close since (about $71.0). Target $101.
- FEIM $84.15: record Q1 revenue of $23.5M (+70%), backlog $129M (+82%), book-to-bill 1.76. The July offering (about $73M) is already done. Jumped 42.4% on Sep 11; 5.5% below its highest close since (about $89.0).
- Avoid KOD (+178% on Sep 28 phase 3 data) and SRZN: biotechs usually sell stock after big data.

Triggers (4 sessions left): enter only on a hold above the post-jump closing high with relative volume of at least 1.5: GNRC above $213, VICR above $292, SEI above $71, FEIM above $89. Stop at the prior post-jump low or -8%, whichever is closer. These are backups to the Micron and Nike plans, not additions on top of them. H-1B book: stock only. Unrestricted book: stock, or calls expiring Oct 9 or later if the spread is under 10% of the premium.

journal.title: Big-mover catalyst scan: method and Sep 29 verdicts
journal.body:
New daily screen (scripts/movers.py): every US stock up 10-15%+ on the day with real volume. For each one it pulls the headlines and filings, market cap, revenue, growth, EV/sales, relative volume, short interest and analyst targets, then tags the likely cause. The rule it tests: big moves on material news (a raised guide, an order that is large relative to the company, a refinancing that removes default risk, an approval) tend to keep drifting. Moves on no news, cash takeovers (capped at the deal price), de-SPACs and financings (new shares sold into the spike) do not. Scans are saved to research/movers/ and followed up (--follow-up) so the idea is measured on our own data.

Sep 29 scan: 44 stocks up 10%+, 23 above $100M market cap. Verdicts:
- IOVA +31.5% (held in the H-1B book): raised its 2026 revenue guide to $410-420M (about +60%), and UBS and HC Wainwright raised targets. A real re-rating. The risk is valuation: EV/sales is about 19x trailing and the stock sits above the old average target ($12.40), so further gains need estimates to keep rising. Hold with the $12.35 stop.
- JELD +12.4% ($1.99, $173M market cap on $3.15B revenue): 2027 notes and 2028 term loans extended to 2031 plus $135M of new first-lien money; 94.5% of noteholders and 72.2% of term lenders committed; no equity in the release. This is the "long-standing problem solved" case. Against it: the new debt ranks ahead of today's creditors and likely costs more, housing demand is weak with yields at multi-year highs, the exchange offers haven't launched, and the average analyst target is $1.93. Re-ratings like this take weeks. Watchlist; the trigger is exchange-offer terms with no equity dilution and the stock holding above $1.90.
- CCL +13.4%: record Q3 revenue, record $7.6B of deposits, raised guidance. A classic post-earnings drift candidate, but a $34B company won't double. Watch for trend days.
- ITG +15.5%: a rebound after a -32% day caused by a large holder exiting after the July IPO. Organic growth is weak and Comcast and Charter are 53% of revenue. Pass.
- WW +13.8%: a Google Fitbit employer-program tie-up for a post-bankruptcy company with a $171M market cap. Small news. Pass for now.
- PWP +11.8%: deal-activity and insider-buying chatter, no hard catalyst. Pass.
- SDEV +108%: no news (the company said so) and -21% after hours. The no-news reversal case in action.
- SANG +37%: cash takeover by BRC, capped. Pass. NAUT +23%: an analyst initiation only. ONEN +22%: de-SPAC on the nuclear theme. BGIN, EGG, SVRN: thin, no fundamental news. All pass.

Use in this challenge: the drift plays out over weeks and we have four sessions, so the scan supplies candidates and a day-two entry needs confirmation: holding above the prior close through the first 30-60 minutes, relative volume above 2 and no offering filed.

journal.title: Plan: four trading days to double
journal.body:
Start: $1,000 cash at Tue Sep 29, 5:45 PM ET. Finish: the Mon Oct 5, 4:00 PM ET close, the same finish line as the H-1B book but one trading day later to start. Target: $2,000, so +100% in four sessions (Wed, Thu, Fri, Mon) plus a weekend of crypto.

The approach: doubling in four sessions needs concentrated, convex bets. That means options on dated catalysts, sized so that one or two hits can double the book, with total losses on the misses accepted. There is no margin at $1,000 (FINRA's $2,000 minimum), so leverage comes from options and 2x/3x ETFs.

Catalyst calendar and instruments:
1. Wed Sep 30, after the close: Micron FQ4. MU Oct 2 options imply about ±7.6% (the at-the-money straddle costs $81). MU contracts cost $700+ even well out of the money, so MUU (2x Micron) Oct 2 calls at $1-3 (about 180% implied volatility) are the sized vehicle. Plan: buy MUU Oct 2 calls (38-40 strikes) for $300-350 at the 9:55 or 10:25 run if MU holds flat or better after the open. Implied volatility usually rises into the print, so buying earlier costs less than buying at 3:55. Skip if MU is down more than 2%. Sell half at Thursday's open on a gap up and the rest by noon Thursday (volatility crush and Friday expiry).
2. Thu Oct 1, after the close: Nike FQ1. NKE Oct 2 options imply about ±8.8%. Sentiment is washed out ("never been more hated"), Jefferies expects a beat, and RBC says a big miss is unlikely. Plan: buy NKE Oct 2 calls (37-38 strikes at $0.75-1.10) for $250-300 near Thursday's close; sell Friday morning.
3. Fri Oct 2: jobs report at 8:30 AM, Tesla Q3 deliveries around 9 AM. Decide at the 8:33 check: SPY/QQQ short-dated options or TSLA/TSLL calls or puts with the proceeds.
4. Weekend: crypto is the only open market. Hold crypto into Monday only with a clear trend or catalyst.
5. Mon Oct 5: final session, everything sold by the 3:40 run.

Tonight: no trades. Crypto has no catalyst-driven setup (BTC $83.4K, -0.1% on the day) and after-hours stock liquidity is thin. Cash waits for Wednesday's Micron setup and any morning news trade.

Risk rules: at most 40% of equity per options catalyst; take profits in thirds (+50%, +100%, and on the catalyst); never hold a contract through its expiration close. Stocks and ETFs use the H-1B book's stops (-15% on 2x ETFs, -12% on stocks). Crypto stop: -8%.
